claims.claim: The mean areas of CaV1.3L and CaV1.3S channel clusters were 2543 ± 50 nm2 and 2119 ± 73 nm2, respectively (n = 7) in tsA-201 cells.
claims.source: The mean areas of CaV1.3L and CaV1.3S channel clusters were 2543 ± 50 nm2 and 2119 ± 73 nm2, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G, n = 7).
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from super-resolution imaging shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claims.claim: The majority (65%) of CaV1.3S clusters underwent at least five stepwise decreases in fluorescence during photobleaching.
claims.source: The majority (65%) of CaV1.3S clusters underwent at least five stepwise decreases in fluorescence, with the remaining clusters showing fewer steps.
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in photobleaching experiments shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: A single photobleaching step was observed in only 4% of the CaV1.3S clusters.
claims.source: A single photobleaching step was observed in only 4% of the CaV1.3S clusters.
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in photobleaching experiments shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: The mean number of CaV1.3S channels per cluster determined through sequential photobleaching was 8 ± 1 (n = 1105 clusters, 18 cells) in hippocampal neurons.
claims.source: The mean number of CaV1.3S channels per cluster determined through sequential photobleaching was 8 ± 1 (n = 1105 clusters, 18 cells) in hippocampal neurons, this number is consistent with the average cluster area calculated from our super-resolution data and is similar to that reported in two different studies on the L-type channel distribution in hippocampal neurons using immunogold-labeling with electron microscopy and high-resolution immunofluorescence techniques (Leitch et al., 2009; Obermair et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from photobleaching experiments and is consistent with previous literature.

claims.claim: Step-photobleaching in tsA-201 cells revealed an average of 5 ± 1 CaV1.3S channels per cluster (n = 585 clusters, 11 cells).
claims.source: Step-photobleaching in tsA-201 cells revealed an average of 5 ± 1 CaV1.3S channels per cluster (n = 585 clusters, 11 cells), consistent also with our super-resolution cluster area measurements (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from photobleaching experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Multi-quantal events detected by imaging Ca2+ influx represent the simultaneous activity of multiple CaV1.3S channels in a membrane microdomain.
claims.source: Collectively, these results support our working hypothesis that multi-quantal events detected by imaging Ca2+ influx represent the simultaneous activity of multiple CaV1.3S channels in a membrane microdomain.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the clustering and photobleaching data.

claims.claim: In cells expressing CaV1.3S-CIBN and CaV1.3S-CRY2 channels, ICa amplitude increased by 35% (n = 6, p<0.001) after blue light illumination.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4C, in cells expressing CaV1.3S-CIBN and CaV1.3S-CRY2 channels, ICa amplitude increased by 35% (n = 6, p<0.001) after illumination, whereas in cells expressing CaV1.3L-CIBN and CaV1.3L-CRY2 channels, there was no change in current amplitude (0.95 ± 0.03 n = 6).
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from optogenetic experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: In cells expressing CaV1.3L-CIBN and CaV1.3L-CRY2 channels, there was no change in current amplitude after blue light illumination (0.95 ± 0.03 n = 6).
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4C, in cells expressing CaV1.3S-CIBN and CaV1.3S-CRY2 channels, ICa amplitude increased by 35% (n = 6, p<0.001) after illumination, whereas in cells expressing CaV1.3L-CIBN and CaV1.3L-CRY2 channels, there was no change in current amplitude (0.95 ± 0.03 n = 6).
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from optogenetic experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Fusing adjacent channels at the tip of their C-tail increases the probability of functional coupling between CaV1.3S adjoined channels but not between CaV1.3L channels.
claims.source: These results suggest that fusing adjacent channels at the tip of their C-tail increase the probability of functional coupling between CaV1.3S adjoined channels but not between CaV1.3L channels.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the optogenetic dimerization experiments.

claims.claim: The normalized conductance and Venus fluorescence exhibited similar sigmoidal voltage dependencies for CaV1.3S channels in 20 mM Ca2+.
claims.source: The normalized conductance and Venus fluorescence exhibited similar sigmoidal voltage dependencies (Figures 5C–D), which can be attributed to the irreversible nature of the Venus reconstitution, resulting in an increased number of fluorescent proteins with each successive depolarization as the open probability of CaV1.3S channels increases.
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in the split Venus experiments shown in Figures 5C-D.

claims.claim: Substituting 2 mM Ba2+ for 20 mM Ca2+ in the external solution led to a robust IBa during membrane depolarization, but caused no accompanying change in Venus fluorescence.
claims.source: Substituting 2 mM Ba2+ for 20 mM Ca2+ in the external solution led to a robust IBa during membrane depolarization, but caused no accompanying change in Venus fluorescence (Figures 5F–I).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in the split Venus experiments shown in Figures 5F-I.

claims.claim: Venus reconstitution was never observed in cells expressing CaV1.3L-VN and CaV1.3L-VC.
claims.source: Importantly, Venus reconstitution was never observed in cells expressing CaV1.3L-VN and CaV1.3L-VC in (see Figure 8).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in the split Venus experiments shown in Figure 8.

claims.claim: CaV1.3S channels can physically interact via their C-termini in response to membrane depolarization, and this association is promoted by intracellular Ca2+.
claims.source: These data indicate that CaV1.3S channels, but not CaV1.3L channels, can physically interact via their C-termini, that this association occurs in response to membrane depolarization, and that it is promoted by intracellular Ca2+.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the split Venus experiments showing Ca2+-dependent but not Ba2+-dependent Venus reconstitution.

claims.claim: Ca2+-induced fusion of CaV1.3S-VN and CaV1.3S-VC increases the activity of adjoined channels.
claims.source: Thus, we tested the hypothesis that Ca2+-induced fusion of CaV1.3S-VN and CaV1.3S-VC increases the activity of adjoined channels by recording CaV1.3S sparklets at a holding potential of -80 mV, in the presence of Ba2+ or Ca2+, before and after applying the same depolarization protocol described above.
claims.evidence: This hypothesis is tested and supported by sparklet recordings shown in Figure 5J-M.

claims.claim: After depolarization, CaV1.3S sparklet activity (nPs) and sparklet density markedly increased in the presence of Ca2+, but not Ba2+.
claims.source: Before depolarization, CaV1.3S sparklet activity was very low (Figure 5J); after depolarization, CaV1.3S sparklet activity (nPs; Figure 5K) and sparklet density (Figure 5L) markedly increased in the presence of Ca2+, but not Ba2+, without a change in the amplitude of the elementary Ca2+ influx (Figure 5M).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in sparklet recordings shown in Figures 5J-M.

claims.claim: Dialysis of MLCKp or co-expression of CaM1234 prevented CaV1.3S-VN and CaV1.3S-VC fusion upon membrane depolarization.
claims.source: Dialysis of MLCKp or co-expression of CaM1234 prevented CaV1.3S-VN and CaV1.3S-VC fusion upon membrane depolarization (Figure 6A–D).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in the split Venus experiments shown in Figures 6A-D.

claims.claim: The fraction of peak ICa remaining at 300 ms (r300) in MLCKp-dialyzed cells (0.11 ± 0.03, n = 5) was similar to that of controls (0.14 ± 0.03, n = 5).
claims.source: Whereas the fraction of peak ICa remaining at 300 ms (r300) in MLCKp-dialyzed cells (0.11 ± 0.03, n = 5) was similar to that of controls (0.14 ± 0.03, n = 5), the rate of inactivation of ICa was slower in cells expressing CaM1234, as reflected in a much higher r300 value (0.75 ± 0.05, n = 5) (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from electrophysiology experiments shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: The rate of inactivation of ICa was slower in cells expressing CaM1234, as reflected in a much higher r300 value (0.75 ± 0.05, n = 5).
claims.source: Whereas the fraction of peak ICa remaining at 300 ms (r300) in MLCKp-dialyzed cells (0.11 ± 0.03, n = 5) was similar to that of controls (0.14 ± 0.03, n = 5), the rate of inactivation of ICa was slower in cells expressing CaM1234, as reflected in a much higher r300 value (0.75 ± 0.05, n = 5) (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from electrophysiology experiments shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: The CaM molecules involved in CDI are distinct from those involved in functional coupling of CaV1.3S channels.
claims.source: Our interpretation of these findings is that the CaM molecules involved in CDI are distinct from those involved in functional coupling of CaV1.3S channels.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of MLCKp and CaM1234 on CDI versus channel coupling.

claims.claim: The coupling coefficient for CaV1.3S sparklet sites in WT cells was 0.07 ± 0.06, whereas that in CaM1234 cells was 0.02 ± 0.02 (n = 5).
claims.source: The coupling coefficient for CaV1.3S sparklet sites in WT cells was 0.07 ± 06, whereas that in CaM1234 cells was 0.02 ± 0.02 (n = 5).
claims.evidence: This is directly calculated from sparklet recordings.

claims.claim: Membrane depolarization increased the coupling coefficient of CaV1.3S channels within multi-quantal sparklet sites in control cells (0.18 ± 0.03, n = 5), but not in CaM1234 cells (0.08 ± 0.05, n = 5).
claims.source: Membrane depolarization increased the coupling coefficient of CaV1.3S channels within multi-quantal sparklet sites in control cells (0.18 ± 0.03, n = 5), but not in CaM1234 cells (0.08 ± 0.05, n = 5).
claims.evidence: This is directly calculated from sparklet recordings.

claims.claim: Depolarization increased CaV1.3 sparklet activity nearly 7-fold in control cells, but had no effect on sparklet activity in CaM1234 cells.
claims.source: However, depolarization increased CaV1.3 sparklet activity nearly 7-fold in control cells, but had no effect on sparklet activity in CaM1234 cells.
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from sparklet recordings shown in Figure 6I.

claims.claim: Ca2+ binding to CaM is required for physical and functional CaV1.3S-to-CaV1.3S channel coupling.
claims.source: Taken together with the ICa and Venus reconstitution results described above, these data strongly suggest that Ca2+ binding to CaM is required for physical and functional CaV1.3S-to-CaV1.3S channel coupling.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experiments with CaM1234 and MLCKp.

claims.claim: CaV1.3-I1608E channels showed a slower rate of inactivation than control and CaV1.3S-AAE channels.
claims.source: CaV1.3S-I1608E channels showed a slower rate of inactivation than control and CaV1.3S-AAE channels (Figure 7B), consistent with the lack of CDI.
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in electrophysiology experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: CaV1.3S-I1608E-VN/VC, but not CaV1.3S-AAE VN/VC, were capable of reconstituting Venus during membrane depolarization.
claims.source: Interestingly, CaV1.3S-I1608E-VN/VC, but not CaV1.3S-AAE VN/VC, which were capable of reconstituting Venus during membrane depolarization (Figure 7C–G).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in split Venus experiments shown in Figures 7C-G.

claims.claim: Binding of CaM to the pre-IQ domain is critically involved in CaV1.3S channel coupling during membrane depolarization.
claims.source: These data suggest that binding of CaM to the pre-IQ domain is critically involved in CaV1.3S channel coupling during membrane depolarization and further supports our previous assertion that the CaM pool involved in CDI is distinct from that involved in channel coupling.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the mutagenesis experiments showing that pre-IQ mutations prevent coupling while IQ mutations do not.

claims.claim: CDI of ICa was faster in cells expressing the CaV1.3L∆116 channels compared to the full length CaV1.3L channels (p<0.05).
claims.source: As expected, CDI of ICa was faster in cells expressing the CaV1.3L∆116 channels compared to the full length CaV1.3L channels (p<0.05; Figure 8B and C).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in electrophysiology experiments shown in Figures 8B and C.

claims.claim: Cells expressing CaV1.3L∆116 channels failed to reconstitute Venus fluorescence with 2 mM Ca2+ in the bathing solution.
claims.source: We found that, with 2 mM Ca2+ in the bathing solution, cells expressing CaV1.3L∆116 channels failed to reconstitute Venus fluorescence, similar to what we observed for the full length CaV1.3L channel (Figure 8D–G).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in split Venus experiments shown in Figures 8D-G.

claims.claim: Even increasing the extracellular Ca2+ concentration to 20 mM was not enough to induce coupling in the CaV1.3L∆116 channels.
claims.source: Even increasing the extracellular Ca2+ concentration to 20 mM was not enough to induce coupling in the CaV1.3L∆116 channels (Figure 8—figure supplement 1, n = 5, p=0.245 -60 mV vs 20 mV).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in split Venus experiments shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Deletion of DCRD is not sufficient to allow coupling of CaV1.3L channels.
claims.source: This result suggests that deletion of DCRD is not sufficient to allow coupling of CaV1.3L channels.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the failure of CaV1.3L∆116 channels to undergo coupling.

claims.claim: Ca2+ sparklets in hippocampal neurons were restricted to specific sites and had multi-quantal amplitudes resulting from the simultaneous opening and closing of multiple channels.
claims.source: As in tsA-201 cells expressing CaV1.3S channels, Ca2+ sparklets in neurons were restricted to specific sites and had multi-quantal amplitudes resulting from the simultaneous opening and closing of multiple channels.
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in sparklet recordings from hippocampal neurons.

claims.claim: The quantal unit of Ca2+ influx in hippocampal neurons was about 40 nM.
claims.source: The quantal unit of Ca2+ influx was about 40 nM.
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from sparklet recordings in hippocampal neurons.

claims.claim: The coupling coefficient (κ) of sparklet sites in hippocampal neurons ranged from 0.14 to 0.33, with an average κ value of 0.23 ± 0.04 (n = 6).
claims.source: The coupling coefficient (κ) of sparklet sites ranged from 0.14 to 0.33. The average κ value was 0.23 ± 0.04 (n = 6).
claims.evidence: This is directly calculated from sparklet recordings in hippocampal neurons.

claims.claim: Sparklet site activity in hippocampal neurons was decreased by application of 300 nM of the dihydropyridine antagonist isradipine and completely eliminated when the concentration of the drug was increased to 10 µM.
claims.source: Importantly, sparklet site activity was decreased by application of 300 nM of the dihydropyridine antagonist isradipine and completely eliminated when the concentration of the drug was increased to 10 µM (Figure 9A and B).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in sparklet recordings shown in Figures 9A and B.

claims.claim: Sparklets in hippocampal neurons were produced by L-type calcium channels.
claims.source: This is consistent with the hypothesis that sparklets in hippocampal neurons were produced by L-type calcium channels.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the sensitivity of sparklets to dihydropyridine antagonists.

claims.claim: CaV1.3 channels have a reduced sensitivity to dihydropyridines compared to CaV1.2 channels.
claims.source: Both CaV1.2 and CaV1.3 channels are expressed in hippocampal neurons (Hell et al., 1993) and although it is impossible to distinguish between these two L-type Ca2+ channels using either electrophysiological or pharmacological methods, it has been shown that CaV1.3 channels have a reduced sensitivity to dihydropyridines compared to CaV1.2 channels (Lipscombe et al., 2004; Xu and Lipscombe, 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claims.claim: 100% of CaV1.2 channels but only ~60% of CaV1.3 channels are inhibited by 300 nM isradipine.
claims.source: A previous study by Koschak et al found that 100% of CaV1.2 channels but only ~60% of CaV1.3 channels are inhibited by 300 nM isradipine (Koschak et al., 2001), given this, it is reasonable to assume that any sparklet remaining after application of 300 nM isradipine is more likely to be generated by CaV1.3channels than CaV1.2.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claims.claim: Near by 25% of the L-type current in hippocampal neurons is carried by CaV1.3 channels.
claims.source: In addition, near by 25% of the L-type current in hippocampal neurons is carried by CaV1.3 channels (Moosmang et al., 2005), this proportion is in agreement with the remaining sparklet site density we observed after the treatment with 300 nM isradipine (Figure 9C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature and is consistent with the experimental observations.

claims.claim: Conditioning membrane depolarization to 0 mV increased sparklet activity nearly 3-fold in hippocampal neurons and induced persistent sparklet activity.
claims.source: As was the case for tsA-201 cells expressing CaV1.3S channels, we found that conditioning membrane depolarization to 0 mV increased sparklet activity nearly 3-fold in the hippocampal neurons and induced persistent sparklet activity (Figure 9D and E).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in sparklet recordings shown in Figures 9D and E.

claims.claim: The coupling coefficient in hippocampal neurons increased from 0.15 ± 0.04 to 0.43 ± 0.12 after membrane depolarization (n = 8).
claims.source: The coupling coefficient increased from 0.15 ± 0.04 to 0.43 ± 0.12 after membrane depolarization (n = 8).
claims.evidence: This is directly calculated from sparklet recordings in hippocampal neurons.

claims.claim: L-type channels undergo cooperative gating, generating persistent Ca2+ influx in hippocampal neurons.
claims.source: These results support the hypothesis that L-type channels undergo cooperative gating, generating persistent Ca2+ influx in hippocampal neurons.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the increased coupling coefficient and sparklet activity after depolarization.

claims.claim: The persistent L-type channels sparklet activity evoked by membrane depolarization in the presence of Ca2+ bears a striking resemblance to the persistent cationic currents observed in several types of neurons.
claims.source: The persistent L-type channels sparklet activity evoked by membrane depolarization in the presence of Ca2+ bears a striking resemblance to the persistent cationic currents observed in several types of neurons (Fransen et al., 2006; Major and Tank, 2004; Moritz et al., 2007; Powers and Binder, 2001).
claims.evidence: This is a comparison to previous literature suggesting a potential physiological relevance.

claims.claim: The somatic and dendritic membranes of neurons expressing both CaV1.3S-VN and CaV1.3S-VC channels displayed prominent Venus fluorescence.
claims.source: We found that the somatic and dendritic membranes of neurons expressing both CaV1.3S-VN and CaV1.3S-VC channels displayed prominent Venus fluorescence (Figure 10A), indicating fusion of CaV1.3S-VN and CaV1.3S-VC channel pairs and functional Venus reconstitution.
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in confocal imaging shown in Figure 10A.

claims.claim: The C-termini of CaV1.3S channels make contact during normal neuronal firing.
claims.source: Since Venus reconstitution is irreversible and neurons have spontaneous electrical activity, this observation suggests that the C-termini of CaV1.3S channels make contact during normal neuronal firing.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of Venus fluorescence in neurons with spontaneous activity.

claims.claim: Expression of CaV1.3S-VN and CaV1.3S-VC channels increased the number of CaV1.3 channel clusters in hippocampal neurons, but not the size of the clusters.
claims.source: We analyzed super resolution images of hippocampal neurons transfected with CaV1.3S-VN and CaV1.3S-VC and found that expression of these channels increased the number of CaV1.3 channel clusters in the cells, but not the size of the clusters (Figure 10—figure supplemental 1).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in super-resolution imaging shown in Figure 10—figure supplemental 1.

claims.claim: The spontaneous fusion of CaV1.3S channels was not a consequence of their being over-expressed in the plasma membranes of the hippocampal neurons.
claims.source: These results indicate that the spontaneous fusion of CaV1.3S channels was not a consequence of their being over-expressed in the plasma membranes of the hippocampal neurons.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that cluster size did not change with overexpression.

claims.claim: Forced coupling of CaV1.3S-CIBN and CaV1.3S-CRY2 channel pairs increased the average firing rate by about 40% (p<0.01) in hippocampal neurons.
claims.source: Forced coupling of CaV1.3S-CIBN and CaV1.3S-CRY2 channel pairs increased the average firing rate by about 40% (p<0.01, Figure 10C).
claims.evidence: This is directly measured from current-clamp recordings shown in Figure 10C.

claims.claim: 488 nm illumination produced no effect on firing rate in control hippocampal neurons transfected only with CaV1.3S-CIBN channels (0.90 ± 0.04, N = 4).
claims.source: 488 nm illumination produced no effect on firing rate in control hippocampal neurons transfected only with CaV1.3S-CIBN channels (0.90 ± 0.04, N = 4).
claims.evidence: This is a control experiment showing that light alone does not affect firing rate.

claims.claim: Adding the L-type calcium channel blocker nifedipine 10 μM to the bathing solution abolished all AP activity after light-induced fusion of CaV1.3S-CIBN and CaV1.3S-CRY2.
claims.source: Adding the L-type calcium channel blocker nifedipine 10 μM to the bathing solution abolished all AP activity after light-induced fusion of CaV1.3S-CIBN and CaV1.3S-CRY2 (Figure 10B, left trace and 10C).
claims.evidence: This is directly observed in current-clamp recordings shown in Figures 10B and 10C.

claims.claim: CaV1.3S channels play a crucial role in regulating the action potential firing in hippocampal neurons.
claims.source: Together, these results highlight the crucial role that CaV1.3S channels play in regulating the action potential firing in hippocampal neurons.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the effects of forced coupling and nifedipine on neuronal firing.

claims.claim: CaV1.3 channels in the plasma membrane of hippocampal neurons are arranged in clusters containing multiple (~8) channels.
claims.source: We have found that CaV1.3 channels in the plasma membrane of hippocampal neurons are arranged in clusters containing multiple (~8) channels.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from super-resolution imaging and photobleaching experiments.

claims.claim: Functional coupling of CaV1.3S channels is promoted by intracellular Ca2+ and involves physical interactions via channel C-termini mediated by physical interactions between Ca2+-CaM and the pre-IQ domain.
claims.source: Functional coupling of CaV1.3S channels is promoted by intracellular Ca2+ and involves physical interactions via channel C-termini mediated by physical interactions between Ca2+-CaM and the pre-IQ domain.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from split Venus, mutagenesis, and CaM inhibition experiments.

claims.claim: Ca2+-driven CaV1.3S channel coupling constitutes a novel feed-forward mechanism for the activation of these channels during membrane depolarization.
claims.source: We propose that Ca2+-driven CaV1.3S channel coupling constitutes a novel feed-forward mechanism for the activation of these channels during membrane depolarization and provides an apparatus for Ca2+-dependent facilitation of inward L-type Ca2+ currents.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: These findings challenge a fundamental tenet of the classic Hodgkin-Huxley model of ion channel gating: that voltage-gated channels open and close independently.
claims.source: Further, these findings challenge a fundamental tenet of the classic Hodgkin-Huxley model of ion channel gating: that voltage-gated channels open and close independently.
claims.evidence: This is a broader implication of the findings regarding cooperative gating.

claims.claim: CaV1.3S channel coupling is critically dependent on intracellular Ca2+ and CaM.
claims.source: Our data suggest that CaV1.3S channel coupling is critically dependent on intracellular Ca2+ and CaM.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from experiments with CaM inhibitors and mutants.

claims.claim: During membrane depolarization, CaV1.3S channels open and Ca2+ flowing through these channels creates a local increase in [Ca2+]i near the mouth and C-terminus of the channel where CaM resides.
claims.source: During membrane depolarization, CaV1.3S channels open. Ca2+ flowing through these channels creates a local increase in [Ca2+]i — a CaV1.3 sparklet — near the mouth and C-terminus of the channel where the Ca2+-binding protein CaM resides.
claims.evidence: This is a mechanistic description based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: Upon binding Ca2+, CaM associates with the pre-IQ domain of the channels, enabling the formation of CaV1.3S-CaV1.3S 'couplets'.
claims.source: Upon binding Ca2+, CaM associates with the pre-IQ domain of the channels, enabling the formation of CaV1.3S-CaV1.3S 'couplets'.
claims.evidence: This is a mechanistic description based on the experimental findings with split Venus and mutagenesis.

claims.claim: The observation of pre-IQ dimers of the structurally similar CaV1.2 channel undergoing coiled-coil interactions in vitro gives credence to this model.
claims.source: The observation of pre-IQ dimers of the structurally similar CaV1.2 channel undergoing coiled-coil interactions in vitro (Fallon et al., 2009) and functionally couples to neighboring channels (Dixon et al., 2015) gives credence to this model.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature on CaV1.2 channels.

claims.claim: Soluble as well as apo-CaM pre-associated with the channel could be involved in inducing physical channel-to-channel interactions.
claims.source: The observation that CaM1234 and MLCKp prevent CaV1.3S coupling would suggest that soluble as well as apo-CaM pre-associated with the channel could be involved in inducing physical channel-to-channel interactions.

results.result: CaV1.3S channels, but not CaV1.3L channels, form functional clusters and undergo cooperative gating. Super-resolution imaging and photobleaching experiments show both isoforms form clusters of similar size (~2100-2500 nm² in tsA-201 cells), but sparklet recordings reveal that CaV1.3S channels have a significantly higher coupling coefficient (κ=0.21±0.05) compared to CaV1.3L (κ=0.08±0.04), indicating cooperative gating occurs specifically in CaV1.3S channels.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C33-C34, C55-C57, C60-C61, and C66 are well-supported by converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches. Super-resolution imaging (C60-C61) demonstrates both isoforms cluster similarly, while sparklet recordings with coupling coefficient analysis (C55-C57) provide quantitative evidence that only CaV1.3S channels undergo cooperative gating. The photobleaching data (C62-C65) confirms multiple channels per cluster. The combination of structural (clustering) and functional (coupling coefficient) data strongly supports the conclusion that clustering is necessary but not sufficient for cooperative gating.

results.result: CaV1.3S channel coupling requires Ca²⁺-dependent binding of calmodulin (CaM) to the pre-IQ domain of the channel C-terminus. Split Venus experiments show that channel coupling occurs only in the presence of Ca²⁺ (not Ba²⁺), and is prevented by CaM inhibition (MLCKp) or dominant-negative CaM (CaM1234). Mutagenesis studies demonstrate that mutations in the pre-IQ domain (AAE mutant) abolish coupling, while IQ domain mutations (I1608E) do not.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C6, C74, C77, C84, C86-C87, and C113-C118 are strongly supported by complementary experimental approaches. The split Venus system (C71-C74, C77) provides direct evidence of Ca²⁺-dependent physical interactions between channel C-termini. CaM inhibition experiments (C77, C84) establish the requirement for Ca²⁺-CaM. The mutagenesis data (C86-C87) precisely identify the pre-IQ domain as the critical binding site. The convergence of optogenetic, biochemical, and mutagenesis evidence provides robust support for this mechanistic model.

results.result: Coupled CaV1.3S channels exhibit increased open probability (Po) and facilitate Ca²⁺ currents. NPo analysis shows Ca²⁺ increases NPo by ~1.5-fold for CaV1.3S but not CaV1.3L channels. Sparklet recordings demonstrate that after depolarization-induced coupling, CaV1.3S sparklet activity (nPs) and density increase markedly in Ca²⁺ but not Ba²⁺.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C47, C50-C51, and C75-C76 are well-supported by quantitative electrophysiological and imaging data. The NPo analysis (C50-C51) provides direct evidence that Ca²⁺ selectively increases channel activity in CaV1.3S. The sparklet recordings (C75-C76) confirm this finding using an independent approach and demonstrate the Ca²⁺-dependence of the effect. The assumption that channel number (N) remains constant during the ~2 min recording period is reasonable and explicitly justified.

results.result: Cooperative gating of CaV1.3S channels increases neuronal firing rates. Optogenetic forced coupling of CaV1.3S-CIBN/CRY2 channels increased action potential firing rate by ~40% in hippocampal neurons, an effect abolished by the L-type channel blocker nifedipine.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C108, and C111 are supported by current-clamp recordings showing a significant (~40%) increase in firing rate upon optogenetic coupling (C108). The control experiment showing no effect of light alone (C109) and the abolition of the effect by nifedipine (C110) strengthen the conclusion. However, the physiological relevance depends on whether the optogenetically-induced coupling mimics naturally occurring coupling, which is not directly demonstrated.

results.result: CaV1.3 channels in hippocampal neurons are organized in clusters containing approximately 8 channels per cluster. Super-resolution imaging shows clusters with an average area of 3660±80 nm², and step-wise photobleaching reveals 8±1 channels per cluster (n=1105 clusters, 18 cells).
results.evaluation: Claims C58, C64, and C112 are well-supported by complementary imaging approaches. The super-resolution data (C58) provides spatial information about cluster organization, while photobleaching (C64) provides quantitative channel counts. The consistency between cluster area measurements and channel counts, and agreement with previous literature using different methods (C64), strengthens confidence in these findings. However, the antibody specificity could not be validated in CaV1.3-KO neurons, introducing some uncertainty.

results.result: Optogenetic forced dimerization of CaV1.3S, but not CaV1.3L, channels increases Ca²⁺ current amplitude. Blue light-induced CIBN-CRY2 dimerization increased ICa by 35% in cells expressing CaV1.3S-CIBN/CRY2 but had no effect on CaV1.3L-CIBN/CRY2 channels.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C70 are supported by optogenetic experiments showing isoform-specific effects of forced dimerization. The 35% increase in CaV1.3S current (C68) with no change in CaV1.3L (C69) provides strong evidence that physical proximity of C-termini is sufficient to enhance CaV1.3S but not CaV1.3L function. This complements the split Venus data and supports the structural specificity of the coupling mechanism.

results.result: The CaM molecules mediating CDI are distinct from those mediating channel coupling. MLCKp dialysis prevented coupling without affecting CDI (r300=0.11±0.03 vs control 0.14±0.03), while CaM1234 expression prevented coupling and reduced CDI (r300=0.75±0.05).
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80 are supported by the differential effects of MLCKp and CaM1234 on CDI versus coupling. The observation that MLCKp blocks coupling without affecting CDI (C78) while CaM1234 affects both (C79) suggests distinct CaM pools. However, this interpretation relies on assumptions about the accessibility and specificity of these inhibitors. Alternative explanations, such as differential affinity or kinetics of CaM binding to different sites, are not fully excluded.

results.result: L-type channels in hippocampal neurons undergo cooperative gating with properties similar to heterologously expressed CaV1.3S channels. Sparklets in neurons show multi-quantal amplitudes (~40 nM quantal unit), coupling coefficient of 0.23±0.04, and depolarization increases coupling from 0.15±0.04 to 0.43±0.12.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C94 and C100-C102 are supported by sparklet recordings in hippocampal neurons showing properties consistent with CaV1.3S channels in tsA-201 cells. The quantal amplitude (C93), coupling coefficient (C94), and depolarization-induced increase in coupling (C100-C101) all match the heterologous expression data. However, the attribution to CaV1.3 specifically (versus CaV1.2) relies on pharmacological sensitivity to isradipine, which is not perfectly selective, introducing some uncertainty.

results.result: Deletion of the distal C-terminal regulatory domain (DCRD) in CaV1.3L is not sufficient to enable channel coupling. CaV1.3LΔ116 channels showed faster CDI than full-length CaV1.3L but failed to reconstitute Venus fluorescence even with 20 mM Ca²⁺.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C91 are supported by split Venus experiments showing that CaV1.3LΔ116 channels, despite having enhanced CDI similar to CaV1.3S (C88), do not undergo coupling (C89-C90). This negative result is important for understanding the structural requirements for coupling. However, the interpretation that DCRD deletion is insufficient (C91) is limited by the fact that CaV1.3LΔ116 still retains a much longer C-terminus (396 aa) than CaV1.3S (183 aa), leaving open the possibility that other regions prevent coupling.

results.result: CaV1.3S channels undergo spontaneous coupling during normal neuronal activity. Neurons expressing CaV1.3S-VN/VC showed prominent Venus fluorescence in soma and dendrites without experimental depolarization, and overexpression increased cluster number but not size.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C107 are supported by confocal imaging showing Venus reconstitution in neurons with spontaneous activity (C104-C105) and super-resolution analysis showing increased cluster density without size change (C106-C107). The inference that coupling occurs during normal firing (C105) is reasonable given the irreversibility of Venus reconstitution and the presence of spontaneous activity. The cluster size analysis (C106-C107) provides important control data showing overexpression does not artificially promote coupling through increased local density.

results.result: CaV1.3L and CaV1.3S channels have similar unitary current amplitudes but differ in their macroscopic current responses to Ca²⁺ versus Ba²⁺. At -30 mV with Ca²⁺, unitary currents were -0.48±0.07 pA (CaV1.3L) and -0.49±0.01 pA (CaV1.3S). CaV1.3L whole-cell current decreased ~40% when switching from Ba²⁺ to Ca²⁺, while CaV1.3S decreased only ~15%.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C37, C41-C42, C44, and C46 are well-supported by single-channel and whole-cell recordings. The single-channel data (C42, C44) demonstrate similar unitary currents between isoforms, while whole-cell recordings (C36-C37, C41) show differential responses to Ca²⁺ versus Ba²⁺. The conclusion that differences in macroscopic currents are not due to unitary current differences (C46) is logically sound. The measurements are consistent with previous literature (C43, C45), providing external validation.

results.result: Sparklets in hippocampal neurons are mediated by L-type calcium channels, likely including CaV1.3. Sparklet activity was reduced by 300 nM isradipine and eliminated by 10 μM isradipine. The remaining activity after 300 nM isradipine is consistent with CaV1.3 channels, which have reduced dihydropyridine sensitivity compared to CaV1.2.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C99 are supported by pharmacological experiments showing dose-dependent inhibition by isradipine (C95). The interpretation that remaining sparklets after 300 nM isradipine represent CaV1.3 activity (C96, C98-C99) is reasonable based on differential sensitivity reported in the literature (C97-C98). However, this remains indirect evidence as the antibody cannot distinguish CaV1.3 from CaV1.2, and pharmacological selectivity is incomplete. The proportion of remaining activity (~25%) matches literature values for CaV1.3 contribution (C99), providing supporting evidence.

results.result: CaV1.3L and CaV1.3S channels have similar activation kinetics. Activation time constants at -10 mV were 1.60±0.22 ms (CaV1.3L) and 1.17±0.051 ms (CaV1.3S), which were not significantly different (p=0.112).
results.evaluation: Claim C49 is supported by direct measurement of activation time constants showing no significant difference between isoforms. This finding is important for the NPo analysis as it validates the assumption that differences in peak current amplitude are not due to faster activation kinetics. The sample size (n=6 for each) and statistical test are appropriate.

results.result: The CaV1.3 antibody used in this study is specific and does not recognize CaV1.2 channels. Previous studies have shown this antibody does not recognize CaV1.2 α subunit in transfected cells or hippocampal tissue.
results.evaluation: Claim C59 is based on citations to previous literature (Hell et al., 1993; 2013) rather than validation in the current study. The authors acknowledge they could not test antibody specificity on CaV1.3-KO neurons. While the cited studies provide some confidence, the lack of direct validation in this study (e.g., using CaV1.3-KO tissue or cells expressing only CaV1.2) introduces uncertainty. The antibody targets the II-III intracellular loop, which may have sequence similarity between isoforms.

results.result: CaV1.3S channels in tsA-201 cells form clusters containing an average of 5±1 channels per cluster. This was determined by step-wise photobleaching of GFP-tagged channels (n=585 clusters, 11 cells).
results.evaluation: Claim C65 is supported by photobleaching experiments in tsA-201 cells. The smaller cluster size in tsA-201 cells (5±1 channels) compared to hippocampal neurons (8±1 channels, C64) is consistent with the smaller cluster area observed in tsA-201 cells by super-resolution imaging (C61). This provides internal consistency between different measurement approaches.

results.result: CaV1.3S channels have distinct biophysical properties compared to CaV1.3L channels, including lower voltage activation, higher open probability, and faster inactivation. These properties are established in the literature and confirmed by the current study.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C18 are supported by citations to previous literature (Bock et al., 2011; Singh et al., 2008; Tan et al., 2011) and confirmed by data in the current study (particularly Figure 1). These are well-established properties of the two isoforms that result from the structural differences in their C-termini. The current study's data are consistent with these prior findings.
